# Direct b-bit OPH backend and hash decision

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

> **Historical artifact:** This records pre-hardening design evidence and does not define the current production method. See `docs/SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md` and ADR 0004.

Date: 2026-08-28

## Decision

The hash decision passes: ntHash2 is the selected production hash candidate for the
next backend iteration. It is strand invariant, has uniform OPH bucket assignment,
matches official vectors, preserves direction semantics, and reduced the complete
CHM13 chromosome 1 Wasm overview build by 19.8% relative to the packed/fmix baseline.

The direct b-bit OPH backend does **not** pass the frozen all-context acceptance
contract. No hash or register tier passed all 15 fixtures. The production UI therefore
remains on its previous packed/fmix backend until the containment failure is resolved;
this report does not authorize a silent backend switch.

## Frozen inputs

The contract is `backend-contract-v1.md`. Raw results are retained in:

* `backend-native.tsv`: 15 synthetic fixtures by 3 hashes by 4 register tiers;
* `backend-chm13-chr1-hor.tsv`: the repeat-rich CHM13 chr1 HOR sample;
* `backend-wasm-chm13.tsv`: repeated full-chromosome release-Wasm timings;
* `backend-smoke.tsv`: smaller-window diagnostic run.

All implementations use the same OPH, HLL, containment, bit-slicing, and matrix code.
Only canonical hash generation changes. The ntHash2 vectors are pinned to official
source commit `c26bd4572a19de81e30d55042dbd33c1fd21d4b6`.

## Native performance

The following values average the 15 default-size synthetic fixtures. Build time is for
both axes; matrix time is the complete 32 by 32 matrix at 1,024 registers.

| Hash | Mean hash-only throughput | Mean build | Mean matrix |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| packed/fmix64 | 173.4 M k-mers/s | 17.58 ms | 0.574 ms |
| ntHash2 | 221.3 M k-mers/s | 16.81 ms | 0.577 ms |
| MashMap MurmurHash3 | 15.0 M k-mers/s | 58.03 ms | 0.578 ms |

ntHash2 was 27.6% faster than packed/fmix in the mean hash-only measurement and 4.4%
faster for the complete native build. Matrix timing is hash independent, as expected.
On the CHM13 HOR sample, packed/fmix and ntHash2 native build times were nearly tied;
the browser measurement below is therefore the selection metric.

## Full CHM13 chromosome 1 in Wasm

Input: RefSeq `NC_060925.1`, 248,387,328 bases. Configuration: self comparison,
1,000 by 1,000 matrix, `k=21`, 1,024 registers, HLL precision 12, 14 comparison bits,
32 verification bits. Measurements are medians of three runs after one warm-up in
Chrome 152.0.7977.64 on the Apple M5 Pro development Mac.

| Hash | Overview build | Matrix | Estimated Wasm state |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| packed/fmix64 | 3,351.5 ms | 285.8 ms | 150,846,442 bytes |
| ntHash2 | 2,687.9 ms | 282.1 ms | 150,846,442 bytes |
| MashMap MurmurHash3 | 33,164.1 ms | 285.4 ms | 150,846,442 bytes |

ntHash2 saved 663.6 ms, or 19.8%, on the decision-relevant complete Wasm build.
MurmurHash3 was 12.3 times slower than ntHash2 in that build.

## Accuracy and hash quality

Across all 180 native candidate rows there were zero false-missing cells, zero
false-present cells, 4,150 correct direction classifications out of 4,150 tested, and
zero observed collisions between distinct 64-bit winners in the 32-bit verification
channel.

At 1,024, 2,048, and 4,096 registers, every hash passed 14 of 15 fixtures. All hashes
and all tiers passed the CHM13 higher-order alpha-satellite sample. At 1,024 registers:

| Hash | CHM13 HOR mean absolute ANI error | p95 | Maximum |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| packed/fmix64 | 0.000857 | 0.002077 | 0.004093 |
| ntHash2 | 0.000904 | 0.002390 | 0.004675 |
| MashMap MurmurHash3 | 0.001131 | 0.002940 | 0.004982 |

The packed/fmix and ntHash2 streams passed a deterministic 1,024-bucket uniformity
test with no observed 64-bit collisions. MashMap's canonicalization takes the smaller
of the two strand hashes. The minimum of two uniform variables is not uniform, and the
raw MashMap hash consequently failed the OPH bucket test (chi-square approximately
44,496 for 1,023 degrees of freedom). It remains a valid bottom-s ordering and oracle,
but is unsuitable as an unmodified OPH register selector.

## Failing context

The failing fixture alternates random sequence, homopolymer, and tandem-repeat blocks.
It creates comparisons in which the core and expanded intervals have strongly
different distinct-k-mer cardinalities. Some cells have high directed containment but
very small Jaccard similarity.

Direct OPH samples Jaccard, then reconstructs containment using the two cardinality
estimates:

```text
intersection = J * (|X| + |Y|) / (1 + J)
containment  = intersection / |X|
ANI          = containment^(1/k)
```

When a small core is contained in a much larger expanded interval, containment can be
high while Jaccard is too small for a fixed register budget to observe a shared
winner. The verification gate correctly prevents a chance b-bit collision from
becoming a false match, but the result can then be zero. The diagnostic fixture
contained a 512-register cell estimated as zero whose exact ANI was 0.982. Increasing
to 4,096 registers greatly improved the distribution but left isolated zero estimates
with exact ANI around 0.71 to 0.73. Hash choice changed which rare cells were missed;
it did not remove the failure.

This is an estimator limitation, not an implementation bug or a hash collision. It
also explains why larger, context-mixed windows and the CHM13 repeat sample looked
excellent while smaller or deliberately cardinality-imbalanced windows did not.

## Required next backend experiment

Given the requirement that sequence context must not create inaccurate window pairs,
plain direct OPH cannot yet be accepted. The recommended next candidate keeps ntHash2
plus bit-sliced OPH for ordinary cells and adds an exact sparse-core containment
channel:

1. Detect low-distinct-cardinality core intervals during the existing stream.
2. Retain their exact canonical hashes within a fixed per-axis budget.
3. In one additional pass over the opposite axis, build postings only for those query
   hashes and compute their directed containment exactly.
4. Use OPH for high-cardinality/high-support comparisons and exact k-mer tiles at the
   finest zoom.

This is not sampling a sample. It is an adaptive exact correction for the specific
size-imbalanced containment case, with memory proportional to sparse query sets rather
than every chromosome k-mer. It requires a new frozen contract and benchmark before
production selection.

Primary references: [ntHash2](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btac564),
[MashMap](https://github.com/marbl/MashMap), and the
[minmers paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btad512).
